scenes.headline: How does a bird this small survive a freezing night?
By day, its heart can hit 1,260 beats a minute.
scenes.body: It has the highest metabolic rate of any warm-blooded animal relative to its size.

scenes.headline: At night it switches almost off.
scenes.body: Torpor: body temperature and heart rate crash, and metabolism falls to a small fraction of normal — a nightly mini-hibernation.

scenes.headline: Then it can fly 800 km non-stop.
scenes.body: A ruby-throated hummingbird nearly doubles its weight in fat, then crosses the Gulf of Mexico in a single flight.

scenes.headline: One sourced wildlife fact, every day.
scenes.body: Save this for the next cold morning.

caption:
A hummingbird's heart can beat 1,260 times a minute. So how does it survive a cold night?

Torpor. It drops its body temperature and metabolism to a fraction of normal until morning — a nightly mini-hibernation. And a ruby-throated hummingbird can still fatten up and cross 800 km of the Gulf of Mexico in one flight.

Source: Cornell Lab of Ornithology (All About Birds). Photos: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — credits shown on screen.
